Hero.description: PyAnimate blends a browser playground, visual execution, guided prompts, and level-based tracks so you can build Python intuition faster.

Outcomes.traceDesc: See variables, loops, and stack transitions instead of reading raw output alone.
Outcomes.practiceDesc: Move through clear tracks with pacing from first syntax to advanced algorithms.
Outcomes.experimentDesc: Edit live, replay execution, and understand mistakes before they harden into habits.

TrackGrid.heading: Progress from first print statement to expert-level reasoning.

LearningJourney.clickHint: Click any step to open the track

AlgorithmPipeline.heading: Every algorithm follows the same pipeline.

LessonSpotlight.heading: See algorithms run, not just read about them.
LessonSpotlight.description: Each lesson animates the execution path step by step, then gives you a challenge to modify and rerun.

Playground.headline: Learn, edit, replay, and understand each step before moving on.
Playground.subheadline: The playground auto-runs on load. Hit {runMyCode} to trace your own Python — every step animated live.
Playground.memoryMatrixHint: Run the timeline to visualize blocks mapping into memory space.

foundation.description: Start from zero. Learn how Python thinks about data, decisions, and flow — step by step, with every concept animated.

beginner.description: Build real programming habits. Master loops, functions, and lists by watching them execute one step at a time.

intermediate.description: Upgrade your toolkit. Explore dictionaries, stacks, queues, and your first search algorithms with visual state tracking.

advanced.description: Think algorithmically. See sorting and tree algorithms animate in real time, understand Big O through observation.

mastery.description: Push to the frontier. Graph search, dynamic programming, and interview-level algorithms — all visualized live.

algorithms.hello-world: Your first Python output. See how print() sends data to the console and why it's the foundation of all debugging.
algorithms.variables-types: Watch a variable come to life in memory. See int, float, str, and bool as living boxes that hold values.
algorithms.string-operations: Strings are sequences. See slicing, concatenation, and methods animate over character arrays.
algorithms.arithmetic: Numbers, operators, and integer division. See exactly how Python evaluates expressions step by step.
algorithms.if-else: Code that makes decisions. Watch execution jump between branches based on truthiness.
algorithms.while-loop: Repetition driven by a condition. See the loop guard check before every iteration and why infinite loops happen.
algorithms.for-loop: Iterate over sequences. See how Python's for loop is really an iterator under the hood.
algorithms.lists-basics: Python's most useful container. See append, pop, and index as operations on an animated memory block.
algorithms.functions-intro: Reusable blocks of logic. Watch a function call push a stack frame and return value flow back to the caller.
algorithms.input-output: Programs that talk to users. See how input() pauses execution and returns a string value.
algorithms.linear-search: Check every element until you find the target. O(n) — the simplest search algorithm there is.
algorithms.count-occurrences: Count how many times a value appears. See a hash map accumulate counts with each pass.
algorithms.find-min-max: Track the running minimum and maximum through a single pass. See why one loop is enough.
algorithms.sum-average: Accumulate values and compute the mean. See the accumulator pattern that powers many algorithms.
algorithms.loop-explorer: Watch how loop iterations update shared state. See score accumulate with each pass.
algorithms.reverse-list: Two-pointer swap from both ends. Watch pointers move inward until they meet in the middle.
algorithms.palindrome: Compare characters from both ends. See how the two-pointer technique confirms symmetry.
algorithms.fizzbuzz: Classic divisibility check. See modulo drive conditional output across 100 iterations.
algorithms.factorial: Multiply from 1 to n. See the product grow step by step and understand why 0! = 1.
algorithms.fibonacci-iterative: Generate the sequence with two rolling variables. See why this beats the recursive version in space.
algorithms.binary-search: Halve the search space every step. Requires sorted input. Watch O(log n) happen live.
algorithms.selection-sort: Find the minimum each pass and move it to the front. See n passes produce a sorted array.
algorithms.insertion-sort: Insert each element into its correct position in the already-sorted prefix. Efficient for nearly sorted data.
algorithms.two-pointers: Use two indices moving toward each other to solve array problems in O(n) instead of O(n²).
algorithms.hash-map-counting: Use a dictionary to count in O(1) per lookup. The foundation of many frequency problems.
algorithms.stack-ops: LIFO in action. See push, pop, and peek animate on a list used as a stack.
algorithms.queue-ops: FIFO in action. See enqueue and dequeue animate and understand why deque beats a list.
algorithms.anagram-check: Are two strings rearrangements of each other? See character counting solve it in O(n).
algorithms.sliding-window: Find the maximum sum in every window of size k. Watch the window glide across the array.
algorithms.merge-sorted: Combine two sorted arrays into one. The core operation behind merge sort.
algorithms.bubble-sort: Compare adjacent pairs. Larger elements bubble to the top each pass.
algorithms.merge-sort: Divide, sort halves, merge. See the recursion tree split and recombine.
algorithms.quick-sort: Choose a pivot, partition around it, recurse. Average O(n log n) with great cache performance.
algorithms.heap-sort: Build a max-heap, extract elements in order. Guaranteed O(n log n) unlike quicksort.
algorithms.bfs: Explore a graph level by level using a queue. Find shortest paths in unweighted graphs.
algorithms.dfs: Explore as deep as possible before backtracking. See the call stack grow with each recursive step.
algorithms.binary-tree-traversal: In-order, pre-order, post-order. Watch nodes visit in different sequences on the same tree.
algorithms.two-sum: Find two numbers that add to a target. See how a hash map turns O(n²) into O(n).
algorithms.valid-parentheses: Use a stack to match open and close brackets. Classic stack application interview question.
algorithms.fibonacci-recursive: See the call tree fan out exponentially. Understand why memoization is essential.
algorithms.dijkstra: Find shortest paths from a source to all nodes using a priority queue. The backbone of GPS navigation.
algorithms.knapsack: Maximise value within a weight limit. See the DP table fill row by row.
algorithms.lcs: Find the longest subsequence shared by two strings. Core of diff tools and DNA alignment.
algorithms.topological-sort: Order tasks respecting dependencies. See Kahn's algorithm remove nodes with zero in-degree.
algorithms.kruskals: Build a minimum spanning tree by greedily adding lowest-weight edges without forming cycles.
algorithms.trie: Insert and search strings letter by letter. See how autocomplete works under the hood.
algorithms.floyd-warshall: All-pairs shortest paths with a 3-loop DP. See the distance matrix update in O(V³).
algorithms.segment-tree: Range queries and point updates in O(log n). See the tree build and propagate sums upward.
algorithms.coin-change: Minimum coins to make an amount. See the DP array fill from 0 up to the target.
algorithms.bit-manipulation: AND, OR, XOR, shifts — the operations behind cryptography, graphics, and competitive programming.

hello-world.title: Knowledge Check
hello-world.question: What does the `print()` function do?
hello-world.successMessage: Correct! print() is used for output.

variables-types.title: Knowledge Check
variables-types.question: Which of the following creates an integer variable?
variables-types.successMessage: Correct! 5 without quotes or decimals is an int.

string-operations.title: Knowledge Check
string-operations.question: Which operator connects two strings in Python?

arithmetic.title: Knowledge Check
arithmetic.question: What does the modulo operator (%) return?

if-else.title: Knowledge Check
if-else.question: Which keyword is used for alternative conditions in Python?

while-loop.title: Knowledge Check
while-loop.question: What happens if a while loop's condition never becomes False?

for-loop.title: Knowledge Check
for-loop.question: Which built-in function is typically used with for loops to iterate numbers?

lists-basics.title: Knowledge Check
lists-basics.question: How do you access the first element of list 'arr'?

input-output.title: Knowledge Check
input-output.question: What type does input() always return?

linear-search.title: Knowledge Check
linear-search.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of Linear Search?
linear-search.successMessage: Correct! Linear Search checks every element — O(n) in the worst case.

count-occurrences.title: Knowledge Check
count-occurrences.question: What does 'count occurrences' do?

options.A: Counts how many times a value appears in the list

count-occurrences.successMessage: Correct! It tallies how often each value appears.

find-min-max.title: Knowledge Check
find-min-max.question: How many passes over the list are needed to find both the minimum and maximum?
find-min-max.successMessage: Correct! One pass is enough to track both min and max simultaneously.

sum-average.title: Knowledge Check
sum-average.question: Which Python built-in returns the sum of all elements in a list?
sum-average.successMessage: Correct! sum(list) adds all elements in a single call.

loop-explorer.title: Knowledge Check
loop-explorer.question: Which Python keyword exits a loop immediately?

reverse-list.title: Knowledge Check
reverse-list.question: What does arr[::-1] return in Python?

options.D: A copy of the list unchanged

reverse-list.successMessage: Correct! The slice [::-1] reverses any sequence in Python.

palindrome.title: Knowledge Check
palindrome.question: A palindrome reads the same...
palindrome.successMessage: Correct! 'racecar' is the same forwards and backwards.

fizzbuzz.title: Knowledge Check
fizzbuzz.question: In FizzBuzz, what is printed for a number divisible by both 3 and 5?
fizzbuzz.successMessage: Correct! Numbers divisible by both print 'FizzBuzz'.

factorial.title: Knowledge Check
factorial.question: What is the value of 0! (zero factorial)?

fibonacci-iterative.title: Knowledge Check
fibonacci-iterative.question: In the Fibonacci sequence, each number equals...

options.B: The sum of the two preceding numbers

binary-search.title: Knowledge Check
binary-search.question: What must be true about an array before applying Binary Search?

options.A: It must have an even length

binary-search.successMessage: Correct! Binary Search requires a sorted array to halve the search space.

selection-sort.title: Knowledge Check
selection-sort.question: In Selection Sort, what happens during each pass?

options.A: The largest element bubbles to the end
options.B: The array is divided in half
options.C: The minimum element is found and swapped to the front

selection-sort.successMessage: Correct! Each pass selects the minimum and places it at the sorted boundary.

insertion-sort.title: Knowledge Check
insertion-sort.question: Insertion Sort is most efficient when applied to...
insertion-sort.successMessage: Correct! Nearly sorted input requires very few insertions, giving O(n) best case.

two-pointers.title: Knowledge Check
two-pointers.question: In a sorted array two-pointer sum problem, if the current sum is too large, what should you do?
two-pointers.successMessage: Correct! Moving the right pointer left decreases the sum.

hash-map-counting.title: Knowledge Check
hash-map-counting.question: What is the average-case time complexity for a hash map lookup?
hash-map-counting.successMessage: Correct! Hash maps provide O(1) average lookup via hashing.

stack-ops.title: Knowledge Check
stack-ops.question: In a Stack, which element is removed first (LIFO principle)?
stack-ops.successMessage: Correct! LIFO — Last In, First Out. The most recently pushed element pops first.

queue-ops.title: Knowledge Check
queue-ops.question: In a Queue, which element is served first (FIFO principle)?
queue-ops.successMessage: Correct! FIFO — First In, First Out. The earliest element dequeues first.

anagram-check.title: Knowledge Check
anagram-check.question: Two strings are anagrams of each other if they contain...

options.A: The same characters in the same order
options.B: The same characters in any order
options.D: Characters that start the same way

anagram-check.successMessage: Correct! Anagrams use identical characters, just rearranged.

sliding-window.title: Knowledge Check
sliding-window.question: The sliding window technique typically reduces time complexity from...
sliding-window.successMessage: Correct! The window slides in O(n) instead of recomputing from scratch each time.

merge-sorted.title: Knowledge Check
merge-sorted.question: Merging two sorted arrays of sizes m and n takes time...
merge-sorted.successMessage: Correct! Each element from both arrays is visited exactly once — O(m + n).

bubble-sort.title: Knowledge Check
bubble-sort.question: After one complete pass of Bubble Sort over an unsorted array, what is guaranteed?

options.B: The largest unsorted element is at its final position
options.C: The array is split in half

bubble-sort.successMessage: Correct! Each pass bubbles the current maximum to its correct final position.

merge-sort.title: Knowledge Check
merge-sort.question: What is the time complexity of Merge Sort in all cases?
merge-sort.successMessage: Correct! Merge Sort always splits and merges in O(n log n).

quick-sort.title: Knowledge Check
quick-sort.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of Quick Sort?
quick-sort.successMessage: Correct! A bad pivot choice (e.g., always the smallest) causes O(n²) worst case.

heap-sort.title: Knowledge Check
heap-sort.question: What data structure does Heap Sort rely on?
heap-sort.successMessage: Correct! Heap Sort builds a max-heap, then extracts elements in sorted order.

counting-sort.title: Knowledge Check
counting-sort.question: What type of input does Counting Sort work best with?

options.B: Integers within a small, known range

counting-sort.successMessage: Correct! Counting Sort is optimal for integers in a bounded range.

recursion-basics.title: Knowledge Check
recursion-basics.question: What prevents a recursive function from running forever?
recursion-basics.successMessage: Correct! Every recursive function must have a base case to stop recursion.

dp-basics.title: Knowledge Check
dp-basics.question: What technique does Dynamic Programming use to avoid recomputing subproblems?
dp-basics.successMessage: Correct! DP stores solved subproblem results to reuse them instead of recomputing.

bfs.title: Knowledge Check
bfs.question: Which data structure does Breadth-First Search use to explore nodes level by level?
bfs.successMessage: Correct! BFS uses a Queue (FIFO) to process nodes in order of discovery.

dfs.title: Knowledge Check
dfs.question: Which data structure does Depth-First Search naturally use (recursively)?
dfs.successMessage: Correct! DFS dives deep first, using a stack (or call stack) for backtracking.

binary-tree-traversal.title: Knowledge Check
binary-tree-traversal.question: Which traversal order visits nodes as Left → Root → Right?
binary-tree-traversal.successMessage: Correct! In-order traversal of a BST produces nodes in ascending order.

two-sum.title: Knowledge Check
two-sum.question: What data structure makes Two Sum solvable in O(n) time?
two-sum.successMessage: Correct! A hash map stores seen values for O(1) complement lookups.

valid-parentheses.title: Knowledge Check
valid-parentheses.question: Which data structure is used to solve Valid Parentheses?
valid-parentheses.successMessage: Correct! A stack tracks opening brackets and matches them with closing ones.

fibonacci-recursive.title: Knowledge Check
fibonacci-recursive.question: What is the time complexity of naive recursive Fibonacci (no memoization)?
fibonacci-recursive.successMessage: Correct! The call tree doubles at every level, giving exponential O(2ⁿ) time.

dijkstra.title: Knowledge Check
dijkstra.question: What is required for Dijkstra's algorithm to produce correct results?

options.B: The graph must be a tree
options.C: All edge weights must be non-negative

dijkstra.successMessage: Correct! Dijkstra fails with negative weights; use Bellman-Ford instead.

bellman-ford.title: Knowledge Check
bellman-ford.question: What advantage does Bellman-Ford have over Dijkstra's algorithm?

options.A: It is faster on dense graphs
options.C: It correctly handles negative edge weights

bellman-ford.successMessage: Correct! Bellman-Ford relaxes edges V-1 times and handles negative weights.

knapsack.title: Knowledge Check
knapsack.question: The 0/1 Knapsack problem is solved using which technique?
knapsack.successMessage: Correct! DP builds a table of optimal subproblem solutions to find the answer.

lcs.title: Knowledge Check
lcs.question: What does LCS stand for?
lcs.successMessage: Correct! LCS finds the longest sequence of characters appearing in the same order in both strings.

topological-sort.title: Knowledge Check
topological-sort.question: Topological Sort is only applicable to which type of graph?
topological-sort.successMessage: Correct! Cycles make a topological order impossible; only DAGs can be sorted.

kruskals.title: Knowledge Check
kruskals.question: Kruskal's algorithm is used to find the...
kruskals.successMessage: Correct! Kruskal's greedily adds the cheapest edge that doesn't form a cycle.

trie.title: Knowledge Check
trie.question: A Trie data structure is most commonly used for...
trie.successMessage: Correct! Tries store strings by prefix, enabling fast prefix lookups.

floyd-warshall.title: Knowledge Check
floyd-warshall.question: Floyd-Warshall computes...
floyd-warshall.successMessage: Correct! Floyd-Warshall finds shortest paths between every pair of nodes in O(V³).

segment-tree.title: Knowledge Check
segment-tree.question: A Segment Tree supports range queries in what time complexity?
segment-tree.successMessage: Correct! Both range queries and point updates run in O(log n).

coin-change.title: Knowledge Check
coin-change.question: Coin Change (minimum coins) is best solved using...
coin-change.successMessage: Correct! DP fills a table of minimum coins for every amount from 0 to target.

bit-manipulation.title: Knowledge Check
bit-manipulation.question: What does x XOR x always equal?
bit-manipulation.successMessage: Correct! Any number XORed with itself is always 0.
